name: Travel-time/distance matrix and isochrone (reachable roads within N minutes)
description: Many-to-many travel times and road distances between up to 25 origins and 25 destinations on a local road dataset (car, walk or bike), or an isochrone: every road segment reachable from one point within N minutes, returned as GeoJSON MultiLineString with its extent and farthest point. Answers "which of these three pharmacies is closest by walking?" and "where can I walk in 10 minutes?".

provenance.reference_values: Fixture graphs are synthetic (CC0). Expected matrices and isochrone counts were produced by installed networkx 3.6.1 dijkstra_predecessor_and_distance on a DiGraph built from the same Skillpack graph builder; the harness checks that installed astar.py and weighted.py are byte-identical to the pinned upstream copies. Graph construction is shared code, so only the search is independently compared.

dataset.description: Dataset name (no folders), e.g. demo_kadikoy or my_pois.csv

budget.enforcement: Raw CLI byte limit and POSIX alarm; strict schema, finite values and nesting checks; MCP subprocess killed/reaped after 10 seconds. One active calculation. Not a hostile-code sandbox.

data.reads: local files by dataset name from SKILLPACK_MAP_DATA or ../map_data

mcp.instructions: Local offline map tool. The dataset is a file NAME inside the folder the user configured (SKILLPACK_MAP_DATA); never invent coordinates or names. Results come from the local data and code; explain them, state data limits (no live traffic) and ask the human to confirm before acting on them. Credit OpenStreetMap contributors when showing OSM-derived data.

limitations: Routing uses only the local road file: free-flow speeds by road class (car: motorway 90 ... residential 25, living street 10, service 15 km/h, or a numeric maxspeed tag), walking 5 km/h (steps 3), cycling 15 km/h (5 on footways that allow bicycles). One-way tags and roundabouts are respected for car and bike, ignored for walking; access=no/private roads are excluded. There is no live or historic traffic, no turn restrictions or turn costs, no traffic lights, ferries, public transport, elevation or time-of-day rules. Vertices are joined only where lines share an identical coordinate (7 decimals), as in OSM-derived exports; bridges/tunnels without shared nodes are not connected. Points are snapped to the nearest routable vertex (straight-line, default limit 300 m), which can be on the wrong side of a barrier. The whole file is read on every call; files above roughly 20 MB may not finish within the 10-second limit. Matrix cells report the distance and time along the path that minimises the chosen metric; null means unreachable. The isochrone lists whole road segments whose both ends are reachable (partial segments at the edge are omitted) and is not a smoothed area; at most 12000 segments are returned, and max_minutes is capped at 60.
port_notes: Single-source Dijkstra is a port of networkx 3.6.1 _dijkstra_multisource with a predecessor dict (as used by dijkstra_predecessor_and_distance): counter tie-break, cutoff pruning and the record of equal-cost predecessors; paths follow the first recorded predecessor, as the harness does. Snapping, profiles and segment listing are Skillpack code (tool/mapdata.py, tool/main.py).
